title: RealNVP coupling Mirror activation views
hypothesis: For task-specific invertible activation transformations generated by a shared RealNVP coupling chart and a 2D latent translation code, sharing the chart and adapting only Mirror codes will recover held-out transformations with lower actual serialized bytes than independent flows and lower query MSE than same/byte-near linear activation steering. A same-budget affine/MLP adaptation may match quality; this is the main counter-hypothesis.
physical_object: shared invertible RealNVP coupling chart (two global scale/shift parameters)
controls: per-task additive linear activation steering (2 parameters/task)
independent RealNVP chart and code (4 parameters/task)
task: Fit generated task transformations from support activations and report query MSE, inverse-cycle error, log-Jacobian consistency, actual inference payload bytes, updates, examples and CPU wall/inference time.

development.selection_metric: development query MSE per actual payload byte; one fixed chart/code configuration, no audit tuning

fresh.split: 8 development task IDs for shared chart fit; 8 support and 256 query activations for each held-out fresh task; task IDs and query inputs seeded separately

paid_objects: every task code or task-specific affine/MLP/flow parameter

success_gate: On at least 2/3 fresh seeds, Mirror query MSE <= 1e-3 and <= 0.25x the linear steering control, inverse-cycle error <=1e-6, payload <=0.6x independent flow and <=0.8x MLP payload. Report whether affine/MLP control matches at comparable bytes; no Mirror-specific claim if it does.
failure_gate: FAIL if query MSE gate or byte gate fails on >=2/3 fresh seeds, invertibility check fails, or a byte-near affine/MLP control matches Mirror within 5% MSE. PROMISING if quality improves but a strict payload gate is narrowly missed.
boundaries: fixed-update learning efficiency does not establish capacity
exact invertibility is not useful task diversity by itself
